findings.title: Materials' 62-point lens gap is extreme
findings.body: Materials sits at the 21st percentile on forward earnings but the 83rd on trailing, a 62-point gap that dwarfs every other sector. The market is underwriting 113 percent earnings growth, which would be a remarkable turnaround from the depressed trailing base.

findings.title: Utilities' forward view ignores trailing collapse
findings.body: Utilities' trailing P/E is at the 1st percentile of its five-year range, yet the forward multiple sits at the 26th. The 25-point gap implies analysts expect earnings to recover, but the implied growth of only 4 percent looks inconsistent with that optimism.

findings.title: Health Care's 44 percent compression is a bet
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E is 19.95 at the 98th percentile, while its trailing multiple is 35.91 at the 78th. The 44 percent compression implies 80 percent earnings growth, an unusually aggressive assumption for a sector already priced at the top of its range.
